text:
Use Tier 3: ensemble the original per-dataset SASRec with the current attentive-similarity model to combine complementary sequential and item-similarity signals. The current model achieves macro validation HR@10 of 0.4725 versus SASRec’s 0.5050, but improves CDs_and_Vinyl from 0.4800 to 0.5250. This suggests complementary behavior worth testing, although category-level results alone do not establish that their errors differ.

Modify model_design and training_evaluation through one atomic change: add a two-branch inference ensemble while retaining each branch’s existing architecture and training objective. Train both branches independently for all four categories using the supplied training splits and seed 42, selecting checkpoints with validation HR@10. Convert each branch’s candidate scores into normalized ranks and average them with a fixed equal weight, avoiding differences in logit scale without fitting additional blending parameters. Evaluate the combined predictions on the same fixed validation users and 99 unique negatives, reporting the equal-weight macro HR@10 without claiming an improvement before measurement.

Update the predictor writer to load both trained checkpoints for the requested dataset and apply exactly the same rank aggregation used during validation. Preserve DATA_DIR, dataset routing, and trial-local artifacts, and run the branches sequentially on one GPU within the execution budget. Leave held-out inference to the host evaluator; this experiment tests whether combining complementary learned rankings breaks the plateau.
